fixes.explanation: Yes, the kingdom. The King says, "Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you…" (Matthew 25:34). Notice the word inherit. An inheritance is handed to you, like a warm batch of cookies somebody else baked.
Land is a fair guess, friend. But the King says, "…inherit the kingdom prepared for you…" (Matthew 25:34). So it's a kingdom, not a plot with a fence. Bigger gift, bigger bakery.

That's the one. The King says, "…I was a stranger and you took Me in…" (Matthew 25:35). Taking someone in means making room for them. I used to do that for every newcomer who slid into the junk drawer I lived in, and it felt good every time.
Whoa, that's not what He says, friend. The King says, "…I was a stranger and you took Me in…" (Matthew 25:35). Sending Him on His way isn't in His list. The ones on the right opened the door.

Right on. They ask, "Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You…" (Matthew 25:37), and then they keep going down the list through the stranger, the naked and the sick and in prison (Matthew 25:38-39). I think they're honestly stunned. It's like me asking where I put my mustache wax. It's on my face. EVERY time.

Nobody asks that, friend. The righteous ask, "Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You…" (Matthew 25:37). Their question is about WHEN they saw Him, not why they weren't told. I think they're surprised, not complaining.

That's right, friend. The King says the eternal fire was "…prepared for the devil and his angels." (Matthew 25:41). He names exactly who it was prepared for. It's heavy stuff, so I'll say it plain and leave it there.
Not quite, friend. In this passage the King says the fire was "…prepared for the devil and his angels." (Matthew 25:41). Baal's prophets don't show up here at all.

True! They say, "Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?" (Matthew 25:44). It's the same kind of question the righteous asked (Matthew 25:37-39). I think both groups were surprised, friend.

It's actually true. The ones on the left say, "Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?" (Matthew 25:44). The righteous asked a question too (Matthew 25:37-39). Both groups ask when they saw Him.

Not quite, friend. The King says, "…whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me." (Matthew 25:45). His answer is about the least of these, and about Him. What wasn't done for them wasn't done for Him.
